summary: USER DESIGN PREFERENCE: one point of view means a complete non-scrollable screen. Fit all page sections in the viewport; do not build a tall page and disable scrolling.
status: Design preference recorded; OCD client home adjusted locally
progress: User explicitly corrected the interpretation: everything should be in one place and visible on one screen, without scrolling. This is a general preference for designing interfaces, not just a request to enable scroll.

decisions: GENERAL DESIGN RULE requested by user: design for one viewport, with all main content and actions visible together. Non-scrollable means the content fits; never achieve this by clipping content or merely hiding scrollbars.
Validate actual section bounds and overlaps at target viewport; a hidden scrollbar alone does not prove the design fits.
Retain meaningful colours and feature-specific file structure.
This correction supersedes the earlier decision to let the desktop home page grow vertically with content.
blockers: None observed for the verified desktop home state
questions: User has not specified an exhaustive minimum device size or how the one-screen preference should apply to long forms and enlarged text. Do not infer permission to clip these.
next: Apply the single-viewport design preference in future design work. Verify content remains visible rather than just disabling scroll.
